cases: Venus takes longer to rotate once on its axis than to orbit the Sun.
Taking creatine supplements prevents Parkinson's disease.

In the SELECT trial, semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% relative to placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease but without diabetes.
protocol.scope: Three live default local reports, actual retrieval, extraction, decomposition, classification, distillation and mapping; owner/public service responses. No HTTP browser/worker test or controlled candidate comparison.
criteria: Population, endpoint, comparator and effect measure preserved
Directional labels justified by available source text
Source roles and independence honestly represented
Access limitations and incomplete evidence visible
Owner/public source ledger and identity agree
protocol.limits: 600 seconds per case; stop on timeout/error; no automatic paid retries

review_type: Agent diagnostic review of all 39 displayed relationships and available source payloads; not blinded human adjudication or a precision score.
excluded_run: tmp/report-quality-pilot: restricted external sockets (WinError 10013), fallback processing; stopped and excluded from quality results.

elements.description: The rotational period of Venus on its axis exceeds its orbital period around the Sun.

findings: One useful comparative element; supported by retained NASA content.
Unmapped YouTube boilerplate labelled full; one mapped source lacks content basis.

elements.description: Creatine supplements are successfully ingested and absorbed by the human body.
elements.uncertainty: No evidence was provided addressing the ingestion and absorption of creatine supplements in the human body.

elements.description: Creatine supplementation produces biological changes in the brain that protect neurological cells from degeneration associated with Parkinson's disease.
elements.uncertainty: Available evidence is limited to preclinical or rat models regarding brain protection mechanisms, lacking direct confirmation in humans.

elements.description: The biological mechanisms induced by creatine directly prevent the development of Parkinson's disease compared to not taking creatine.
elements.uncertainty: Extensive clinical trial data contradicts the claim that creatine prevents or slows Parkinson's disease.

findings: Vacuous ingestion/absorption element and unrequested mechanistic premise.
Progression/treatment evidence used as challenge to onset prevention; uncertainty conflates endpoints.
Preclinical mechanism sources correctly contextual; 14 of 21 sources snippet-only.

elements.description: The SELECT trial was conducted on a population consisting of adults with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease without diabetes.
elements.uncertainty: Trial inclusion criteria defined overweight/obesity as BMI ≥27 kg/m² with prior cardiovascular events rather than general population obesity.

elements.description: Semaglutide administration resulted in a causal reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events relative to placebo within the SELECT trial cohort.
elements.uncertainty: Reductions were observed over a mean follow-up of 40 months when added to standard secondary cardiovascular prevention care.

elements.description: The magnitude of the reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events achieved by semaglutide was exactly 20% compared to the placebo group in the SELECT trial.
elements.uncertainty: The 20% figure represents relative risk reduction (HR 0.80 with 95% CI 0.72-0.90), corresponding to an absolute risk reduction of 1.5% (6.5% vs 8.0%).

findings: Relative-effect wording dropped and exactly added to magnitude element.
Original trial result unavailable in retained introductory NEJM snippet.
SCORE association mapped as causal support for SELECT; cited background counted as primary and apparent alternate publication hosts counted separately.

decision: Not ready for 8/10 reassessment or candidate activation. Next bounded correction: decomposition and population/endpoint/study-design fidelity, preserving sources.
